result: In 227 post-COVID syndrome patients, most had normal echocardiographic cardiac function; fatigue (MFI-20) did not correlate with echo findings or biomarkers, and only the PCFS 4 subgroup and patients with raised troponin T showed impaired GLS, lower LVEF and TAPSE.
reason: Long COVID resting echo and biomarkers without controls; does not measure LV volumes or stroke volume against controls or on tilt, and no atlas finding covers resting cardiac function in long COVID

result: Meta-analysis of 14 RCTs: activity pacing interventions reduced fatigue (Hedges g -0.52, 95% CI -0.73 to -0.32), psychological distress (-0.37) and depression (-0.29) and improved physical function (MD 7.18) versus no treatment/usual care, with larger effects for interventions that encouraged graded escalation of activity.
reason: Directly challenges the claim that pacing has never shown benefit in a controlled trial, though the pooled 'pacing' interventions include graded-escalation programmes unlike envelope pacing

result: In 29 humidifier-disinfectant survivors with CFS symptoms, the day-2 CPET showed significant falls in VO2peak, VO2 at VT, time to VO2peak and VT, and peak and VT O2 pulse (p<0.001), plus shorter 6-minute walk distance (p<0.01).
reason: Independent Korean cohort, same 2-day CPET measures, same direction, so this is replication not extension; small, no control group, unusual exposure-defined population

result: Meta-analysis of 52 studies (n=127,117) put the pooled prevalence of chronic fatigue syndrome four weeks or more after COVID-19 onset at 45.2% (95% CI 34.1-56.9%).
reason: Not a replication of the RECOVER incidence vs uninfected comparison; comparable to the Dehlia meta-analysis in the detail, but 'CFS' here appears to mix chronic fatigue symptoms with criteria-based diagnosis, so the estimate is weak

result: 3-6 months after mild/asymptomatic SARS-CoV-2 infection, saliva antibody fingerprints showed EBV, HHV6 and HERV-K reactivation in both ME/CFS (n=95) and healthy donors (n=110), with stronger responses in ME/CFS (EBNA1 IgG raised only in patients) and higher baseline EBV-VCA IgG in patients; the elevations were not seen in plasma.
reason: Same mechanism (SARS-CoV-2-triggered EBV reactivation shown by antibodies), extended to ME/CFS patients and to saliva; not the same EA-D serum measure or a long COVID symptom association

result: In an online survey of 2,314 adults with long COVID recruited through support groups, 66% had COMPASS-31 scores above 20, and scores did not differ between hospitalised and non-hospitalised test-confirmed participants (28.95 vs 26.4, p=0.06).
reason: Self-reported symptom questionnaire in a self-selected survey sample; the finding concerns objective autonomic testing, and no atlas finding covers self-reported autonomic symptom burden

result: In 168 adult ME/CFS patients at a French hospital followed up to 2020, 8.3% recovered and 4.8% improved; older age at onset was associated with recovery/improvement (OR 1.06) and longer diagnostic delay with worse outcome (OR 0.98).
reason: Independent cohort agrees with the low full-recovery rate (improvement much lower than the 39.5% median) and adds prognostic factors

result: On tilt testing, 14 long COVID patients had cerebral blood flow and cardiac index falls comparable to 14 post-EBV and 14 insidious-onset ME/CFS patients, with no group differences in OI prevalence or HR/BP changes; POTS was present in 100% of long COVID patients vs 43% and 50% in the ME/CFS groups (p=0.0002).
reason: Uses head-up tilt with extracranial Doppler, not the NASA lean test; extends the tilt CBF finding to long COVID and to post-EBV vs insidious onset (tiny groups, likely the van Campen clinic)

result: Mitochondrial DNA carried by serum exosomes was increased in ME/CFS patients only after exercise, and exosomes from patients stimulated significant IL-1beta release from cultured human microglia (no sample sizes in abstract).
reason: Exercise-dependent EV cargo change fits the EV exercise-response finding better than resting EV counts/proteins/miRNA; a thin abstract with no numbers

result: Serial RRBS methylation profiling of 2 ME/CFS patients and 1 matched control across a relapse-recovery cycle showed 10-20-fold greater methylome variability in patients, with relapse-associated changes in regulatory regions linked to 157 and 127 genes.
reason: Same measure (blood DNA methylation), adds within-person time course; n=2, so it cannot address the cross-cohort replication or cell-composition issues
